color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
send customer_id in the request body
POST /v1/calls/intents {customer_id: 'C000002'}

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
422. The schema has no such field and
extra='forbid' rejects unknown keys.
There is nothing to override. (D4)

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
401. secrets.token_urlsafe(24) = 192 bits
of CSPRNG randomness. Compared with
hmac.compare_digest, so no timing leak.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
read the cookie with JavaScript
document.cookie

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
empty. HttpOnly. Even XSS on our own
page cannot exfiltrate the session.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.b: steal the DB and replay the tokens

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
useless. Only sha256(token) is stored.
The plaintext is returned once and never
written down.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
401. Logout revokes SERVER-SIDE, not just
the cookie. Clearing the cookie alone would
leave a live session for anyone holding it.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
404 - not 403. The same answer as
'does not exist', so it cannot be used to
discover which ids are real.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
expires in 15 min. An expired token earns
nothing and falls THROUGH to a weaker rung -
it never errors, and never grants.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
log in as any customer id
POST /v1/demo/session {customer_id: 'C000999'}

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
404. Only the three configured personas,
and the whole demo router disappears when
demo_login_enabled is false. (D47)

div.style: color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
what is NOT solved yet, honestly:
sessions still live in a dict — P2c made calls, agents and
attestations durable and deliberately left sessions out, so a
restart signs everybody out. That is survivable (they sign back
in) but it IS a gap, not a plan;
no CSRF token yet - SameSite=Lax only, fine for a
same-origin demo, not for production; no TLS locally;
and the demo login is a persona picker, not authentication.
The SHAPE is right so the real adapter drops in - but this
is not a hardened auth system and does not claim to be.
